precepts.text: It shall be the prince's part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. The meat and drink of Colossians 2:16 are these offerings.
precepts.point: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days. The meat is the meat offerings and the drink is the drink offerings; do not let a Christian use this verse to say it is talking about eating pork or getting drunk. This is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said.
precepts.why:
Christians use the meat in Colossians 2:16 to say you can eat pork, and the drink to say you can get drunk. It is not talking about that. Stop listening to these dumb Christians, especially if they are black or Latino; never listen to them.

Ezekiel explains it: “And it shall be the prince’s part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the house of Israel”. See that: meat offerings, drink offerings, in the feasts, the new moons and the sabbaths, the very same list as Colossians 2:16.

“he shall prepare the sin offering, and the meat offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.” These offerings were made for reconciliation. So Paul’s words read: let no man judge you in meat offerings, or in drink offerings, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, because the reconciliation those offerings pointed to is in Christ.

precepts.text: The sin offering, meat offering, burnt offering, and peace offerings were prepared to make reconciliation for the house of Israel; that is what reconciled means.
precepts.point: The letters of Paul were written to Israelites living in those lands and called by their names, Romans and Corinthians, the same way we are called American or Jamaican today; written today they would be the letter to the Jamaicans or the letter to the Puerto Ricans.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
This is what reconciled means. The prince “shall prepare the sin offering, and the meat offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.”

The sin offering, meat offering, burnt offering, and peace offerings were prepared to make reconciliation for the house of Israel, and the trespass offering’s atonement in Leviticus 6 is the same work: bringing the nation that had become the Most High’s enemy back together with its God.

precepts.text: The sin offering and the burnt offering were prepared to make reconciliation for the house of Israel; the purified altar carried that reconciliation.
precepts.point: The fat, the caul, and the kidneys, the guts, were burnt upon the altar, but the bullock with his hide and flesh was burnt with fire without the camp. Christ's crucifixion lines up with the law of sacrifice: he was taken outside Jerusalem to the place called Golgotha and crucified there.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
Moses put the blood upon the horns of the altar, purified the altar, and sanctified it, to make reconciliation upon it. Reconciliation goes back to what the prince prepares: “the sin offering, and the meat offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.”

The purified altar carried that reconciliation for the house of Israel. And the bullock with his hide and flesh burnt with fire without the camp lines up with Christ’s crucifixion: he was taken outside Jerusalem to the place called Golgotha and crucified there.

precepts.text: It is the prince's part, the Levites, to give the burnt offerings and make reconciliation for the house of Israel.
precepts.point: They ministered before the tabernacle of the congregation with singing until Solomon built the house of the Most High, and then they waited on their office according to their order, showing the tribe was in right order at this time.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

precepts.why:
“And it shall be the prince’s part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the house of Israel”, and “to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.” It is the prince's part, the Levites, to give the burnt offerings and make reconciliation for Israel.

The singers David set over the service of song were of that tribe. “And they ministered before the dwelling place of the tabernacle of the congregation with singing, until Solomon had built the house of the Lord in Jerusalem: and then they waited on their office according to their order.” The tribe was in right order at this time.
